properties.description: A striking Neoclassical villa in tranquil gardens on Hampstead Heath, Kenwood boasts breath-taking interiors by Robert Adam and a world-class art collection.

images.title: Rembrandt's Self-Portrait with Two Circles is one of Kenwood's great masterpieces (English Heritage)
The Entrance Hall at Kenwood (English Heritage)
The Music Room at Kenwood, home to Georgian beauties by Gainsborough and Reynolds (English Heritage)
Enjoy a stroll along Kenwood's iconic south terrace (English Heritage)
Marvel at Dutch and Flemish Old Masters in the east wing (English Heritage)
'The Guitar Player' is one of only 36 paintings by Vermeer in the world (English Heritage)
Lady Mansfield's 18th-century tea room at the dairy (English Heritage)
Learn how English Heritage cares for Kenwood and see some conservation in action (English Heritage)
The Robert Adam designed library at Kenwood (English Heritage)
The Creamery at Kenwood's 18th-century dairy (English Heritage)

properties.description: Grade II-listed Georgian domestic building c.1760, formerly part of the Bedford Estate. Interior refurbished 1925 to form lecture hall (restored 2014), library, bookshop and offices. Oak woodwork and green Doulton tiles line the staircase.

images.title: Bust of Swedenborg by Preston Powers (1879) - James Wilson
Stained glass window image of Swedenborg, vestibule (detail) - James Wilson

properties.name: The Swedenborg Society

properties.description:
Striking, provocative and one of London’s few Grade I listed post-war buildings – welcome to architect Denys Lasdun’s award-winning design. We invite you to drop in, take an expert tour, explore our archives and museum, get creative and more to discover the Royal College of Physicians' London home. 

See https://history.rcp.ac.uk/event/open-house-festival-2026 for more.

images.title: View from the Medicinal Garden - Gail Chapman

properties.name: Royal College of Physicians

properties.description: A rare example of Thomas Archer's work and a masterpiece of English Baroque, originally dubbed Queen Anne's Footstool. A Grade I listed building, restored by Marshall Sisson after extensive bombing damage, now a busy concert hall.

images.title: The East Side of the Square

properties.name: Sinfonia Smith Square

properties.description: 6-storey building featuring a Western exterior and traditional Islamic interior, modelled on the Blue Mosque in Istanbul. Has dome and minaret tower.
properties.name: Suleymaniye Mosque

properties.description: During Open House, the Friends of Battersea Parish Church present a Floral Festival, organ recitals, historical displays, alongside 3 talks exploring history, creativity, sanctuary & Battersea’s radical past. Sat 12 Sept Dr. Peter Rumley at 6pm, Tues 15 Guy Stagg at 6.30pm,  Thurs 17 at 6.30pm Rory Walsh & Mike Squires.  Plus Join us for Choral Evensong amidst the flowers at St Mary’s Battersea.
properties.name: St Mary's Church, Battersea

properties.description: The church (1822 - Grade I listed) is an early and important example of Greek Revival architecture in London. Significant features include the caryatids and tower copied from models in Athens, and the atmospheric crypt.
properties.name: St Pancras Church & Crypt

properties.description: St Anne's Limehouse has been described as 'the finest parish church in England.' Designed by Nicholas Hawksmoor, it is Grade I listed and one of the Major Churches in the Church of England. It is home to a thriving Christian congregation.

images.title: Our exhibition of tapestries made for the Millennium - in our galleries over Open House week
CfSA run regular exhibitions - the current exhibition is about the Original Chinatown of London

properties.name: St Anne's Church, Limehouse

properties.description: Loughborough Pearson's red brick building is unimposing from the outside, but inside is a riot of Gothic Revival design. Golden mosaics reveal the character of the Grade II* listed chapel, built as part of the Middlesex Hospital.

images.title: The ornate baptisery of the Fitzrovia Chapel

properties.name: Fitzrovia Chapel

properties.description: London's pre-eminent Victorian Jewish cemetery, now transformed into a heritage attraction. The "House of Life"  shares stories of a community and remarkable biographies through guided walks and events.

images.title: Prayer Hall at Willesden Jewish Cemetery.  Miriam Marson
Harriet Samuel Grave at Willesden Jewish Cemetry. Miriam Marson.

properties.name: Willesden Jewish Cemetery

properties.description: The Stirling-prize shortlisted King’s Cross Masterplan established a framework for the incremental redevelopment of this industrial heritage site through a mix of uses and a network of public spaces structuring new urban blocks and knitting the site into its context.

images.title: Granary Square at King's Cross. Courtesy of John Sturrock and Related Argent
Bagley Walk at King's Cross. Courtesy of John Sturrock and Related Argent

properties.name: King's Cross Masterplan

properties.description: Wren designed building of 1675, interior lost in blitz of 1940, reopened 1957 with 'Wren inspired' interior
properties.name: St Bride's Church, Fleet Street

properties.description: A guided walk through Home Park Water Meadows with Thames Landscape Strategy. It is the site of a wetland restoration project that has increased biodiversity and sustainability on the historic site. It is not usually open to the public.
properties.name: Flood Meadows at Hampton Court

properties.description: Start at Stamford Brook tube.  Follow the hidden river, Stamford Brook, through streets and parks.  Amongst the architecture we will see on this route is a delightful square with great variety.  Finish near Hammersmith Station.

images.title: Map of course of Stamford Brook

properties.name: Stamford Brook walk

properties.description:
Come and see our light filled Studio & Office space and find out more about what we do at The Photography Foundation! 

Browse our Trainee photography zines and meet our welcoming Staff Members.

images.title: THE PHOTOGRAPHY FOUNDATION STUDIO,  Entrance to the building
THE PHOTOGRAPHY FOUNDATION STUDIO,  View from other side - our studio is on the second floor

THE PHOTOGRAPHY FOUNDATION STUDIO,  Exterior amongst other buildings
THE PHOTOGRAPHY FOUNDATION STUDIO,  The Photography Foundation Entrance

properties.name: The Photography Foundation Studio, Design District (D2)

properties.description:
Andaz London Liverpool Street, a concept by Hyatt, blends rich history dating back to the 1200s with modern decor and the vibrant energy of its London neighborhood.

Step inside and join us for an open house tour led by our dedicated team!
properties.name: Andaz London Liverpool Street

properties.description: A floating acoustic architecture, playfully reframing public space as an essential community engagement through sound & site mapping. Accessed by smartphone, headphones & echoes.xyz app, the Pavilion is located outside the Serpentine Gallery,. Drawing on Oskar & Zofia Hansen’s Open Form architectural concept it is one of 15 in a series including Venice, Berlin, Dublin, Bergen and Arctic Norway.

images.title: Architectural and spatial design functions also as logo for London Pavilion audiowork
QR code to access London Open Form Pavilion of Air
Architectural design & spatial sound design for Pavilion with position in Kensington Gardens

properties.name: London Open Form Pavilion of Air

properties.description: Guided walking tours of the grounds of Bethlem Royal Hospital, taking in the Hospital's historic Chapel, its beautiful grounds, the GUTS Cafe, Bethlem Museum of the Mind, and Bethlem Gallery.
properties.name: Bethlem Royal Hospital

properties.description: Morris+Company is an award-winning architecture practice based in Hackney, east London. We have applied circular economy principles to the retrofit of our own studio, gallery and café space on Mare Street, reducing waste, reusing materials, and designing for longevity.  We place the creative ‘act’ of architecture onto the high street, reveal our practice to the public and engage local communities.
properties.name: Morris+Company | 'Waste Not: Materials, Making and the Circular Economy' Exhibition

properties.description: The Grade I listed North Wing at St Bartholomew’s Hospital in the City of London houses two of England’s most important interiors, the Great Hall, and the Hogarth Stair with its large paintings by William Hogarth. The hospital was designed by architect James Gibbs and construction of the North Wing was completed in 1732.
properties.name: St Bartholomew's Hospital

properties.description: The Grade II listed Victorian complex, originally built between 1865 – 1906, is one of London’s most iconic civic buildings. After a devastating fire in 2013, it was placed in the Heritage at Risk Register and closed. Now, after sensitive restoration by Feix & Merlin and General Projects, it reopens its doors. With a modern CLT extension that celebrates its former glory while embracing its future.

images.title: View of Walworth Town Hall from Walworth Square

properties.name: Walworth Town Hall

properties.description: St Anne's Church, a SW London landmark, nicknamed Pepperpot, celebrated its bicentenary in 2024 (Robert Smirke 1824). The church will be open September 15, 17 and 18 for guided tours and exhibits from the archives.
properties.name: St Anne's Church Wandsworth

properties.description: St James's Piccadilly is a Grade I listed Christopher Wren church in the heart of the West End. Completed in 1684, and known as the Artists' Church, its interiors include historic works of art by Grinling Gibbons (reredos, organ case and font), postwar Classical interiors by Albert Richardson, and contemporary art by Che Lovelace honouring the 18th-century abolitionist Quobna Ottobah Cugoano.

images.title: St James's Church Piccadilly, seen from Jermyn Street
The lime wood reredos carved by Grinling Gibbons
The River (left) and Passage (right) by Che Lovelace hanging in the narthex at St James's Piccadilly

properties.name: St James's Piccadilly

properties.description: The Croydon Urban Room is a space to talk about the past, present and future of the Croydon town centre. Through conversa­tions, stories, exhibitions and events, the Urban Room brings together the views of those who live, work and visit the area to create a shared vision of the future and test new uses live in action.
properties.name: Croydon Urban Room

properties.description: London is the world's first National Park City, and our visitors centre at 80 Mortimer Street is the entry point to hundreds of places to visit and things to do across a greener, healthier and wilder London.

images.title: London National Park City visitors centre at 80 Mortimer Street around the corner from Oxford Circus

properties.name: London National Park City Visitors Centre

properties.description: We are a theatre company for performers and artists with learning disabilities in the West London area. We will put on an exhibition of artworks and costumes at our Community Arts Centre.

images.title: Art exhibition. Image credit: IMPACT Theatre

properties.name: IMPACT Community Arts Centre

properties.description: A revival and love letter to London’s lost bohemia. Travel back in time to the legendary haunt of some of Soho's greatest creatives.   Featuring pictures, press cuttings and even the piano from the much loved private members club.
properties.name: Explore the authentically recreated Colony Room

properties.description: Resonance FM is a pioneering, non-profit community radio station, with a studio at 7 Risborough Street, Southwark, London. Broadcasting 24/7 on 104.4 FM, DAB, and online, it offers over 100 weekly shows created by volunteer engineers and programme-makers. The station champions free expression and artistic diversity, providing a platform for local and international voices across arts & culture.
properties.name: Resonance FM Studios

properties.description: Flux Innovation Lounge opens its doors for Open House Festival, inviting visitors to explore where physical, virtual and immersive worlds meet. Described as one of London’s most celebrated creative venues and a hotbed for innovation and technology, Flux is a working innovation space where ideas are tested, experienced and brought to life. Join us to discover the future of the built environment.
properties.name: Flux Innovation Lounge, Greenwich Design District

properties.description:
The building of Worlds End Studios started life as a factory manufacturing machines for commercial baking ovens; it burned down and the remains were used as the foundations of what we know today.
Two young architects found the ruined site in 1974. They wanted to create a community workspace geared toward designers, one of the first of its kind, in London.

images.title: Old vs New Elevation of Worlds End Studios

properties.name: Worlds End Studios

properties.description:
A curious and enlightening wander through the City of London led by an expert guide. If you know where to look, the past still communicates its secrets concealed within a city that is 2000 years old.

We'll discover clues to the City’s past in strange marks and curious symbols along the route, keeping an eye out for honeybees, demi-maidens and sunbursts.
properties.name: Secrets and Symbols of the City

properties.description: Explore a fascinating working-class neighbourhood with a radical and surprising past. Learn of its efforts to hold onto its distinctive and proud culture in the face of rapid gentrification, especially within the neighbouring St Pancras and King's Cross districts. Discover the place of nature, community, heritage, and wellbeing in a neighbourhood that's changing very rapidly.

images.title:
The People's Museum Somers Town. 
Photo @meetmrlondoner.

Edith Neville Primary School, Somers Town. 
Photo @meetmrlondoner.

properties.name: Somers Town folk

properties.description: Medieval industry, imperial trade, immigration, poverty, wartime destruction and modern regeneration have all left their mark on the Limehouse area. This walking tour covers a range of architects and architecture from C18th to C21st.
properties.name: From Limehouse to Canary Wharf

properties.description:
An interactive workshop inviting residents and visitors to reimagine the public spaces around them using art and simple architecture techniques.

Open to children, families, and older residents, the workshop encourages intergenerational dialogue, bringing together youthful imagination and lived experience to explore the community's creativity.
properties.name: Reimagining Play in London's Green Spaces

properties.description: Walking tour of the sites of the last days of King Charles I and the legacy of the upheavals which cost him his life and still echo to this day.
properties.name: Walking Tour:  Charles I - Monster or Martyr ?

properties.description: Visit the Grade II listed Corbett Community Library building. This beautifully preserved Edwardian building is rich in architectural character and heritage, featuring stunning stained glass windows, an impressive dome, ornate door handles, and a historic brass plaque. Discover the history and craftsmanship of this remarkable community landmark during your visit.

images.title: The library building, photographed by Rachel Braithwaite,
Glass dome, photographed by Rachel Braithwaite
Outside of the building in full by Rachel Braithwaite

properties.name: Corbett Community Library
